name: 'Azîzî
bio: 'Azizi was the pen-name of a certain Mustafa of Constantinople, who held the appointment of provost of the Seven Towers and is known mainly from his Shehr-engiz.
The poems here are taken from E. J. W. Gibb's Ottoman Poems (1882), the first English verse translations of Ottoman poetry; dates and biographical details follow Gibb's Biographical Notices.

poems.title: Zemân the Long-Haired
poems.author: 'Azîzî
poems.note: From his Shehr-engiz. Sachli Zeman (Fortune the Long-haired).
poems.text:
Zemân the Long-haired, 'midst these lovely ones see,
A wayward, wanton Torment of the world she.

Like Fortune, she nor clemency nor grace knows;
The number of her hairs her lovers' tale shows.

The tribute from the realm of hearts her curls bore,
Seduced me have these locks that hang her neck o'er.

poems.title: She Whom They Call Jihân's a Damsel Moon-Faced
poems.author: 'Azîzî
poems.note: From his Shehr-engiz. Jihan Banu (Lady World).
poems.text:
She whom they call Jihân's a damsel moon-faced,
Who, like the World, is faithless, and doth hearts waste.

Save faithlessness, though comes not from the World aught;
The heart from that love of the soul can pass not.

Let but her mind contented be with poor me,
Then may the World divorced from me for aye be.

poems.title: La'l-Pâra as Her Name Doth One of These
poems.author: 'Azîzî
poems.text:
La'l-Pâra as her name doth one of these own,
A girl whose heart is hard as is the flint-stone.

Her mouth in very truth 's a ruby bright red,
Her teeth are pearls, so too the words by her said.

Strange were it, if my heart be by her love slaved?
For sooth her rubies bear the "coral-prayer" graved.

poems.title: And Aq-'Alem They One of Yonder Maids Call
poems.author: 'Azîzî
poems.text:
And Aq-'Alem they one of yonder maids call,
For her the moon of heaven acteth jackal.

Is't strange if through her loveliness she famed be?
A white Rose on the earth is yonder Hürî.

He who with that bright Moon as friend goes,
A universe enjoys more fair than earth shows.
